newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Q1 tobacco sales fall 7.3 pct in volume.
newsitem.headline: French Q1 tobacco sales fall 7.3 pct in volume.

text.p: Tobacco sales fell 7.3 percent in volume in the first quarter of 1997 but price increases resulted in flat sales figures, the Tobacco Documentation and Information Centre (CDIT) said on Thursday.
Overall sales of tobacco products totalled 20,970 tonnes compared to the 22,632 tonnes sold during the comparable 1996 period, the centre said.

In financial terms, first-quarter sales totalled 17.07 billion francs versus 17.08 billion francs during the first three months of 1996. Some 12.86 billion francs of the total were turned over to the state in the form of taxes.
Cigarette sales fell 8.2 percent to 18.8 billion units from 20.5 billion during the first quarter of 1996, including 14.2 million of blond tobacco and 4.6 million of brown tobacco, the CDIT said.
Cigar sales fell 2.5 percent to 343.6 million units while sales of loose tobacco for pipes and hand-rolled cigarettes rose 2.9 percent to 1,693.5 tonnes.
The centre said sales typically fall after a major price increase. Cigarette prices went up nine percent last December 20.
Over the past five years, prices have increased, on average, 96 percent, the centre said.
